body:
Triage: type `Bug` (declared ≠ enforced — the repo's stated queue model, "the full suite blocks", is measurably not enforced on `77da09bac`). Stays `needs-user-decision`: branch-protection / merge-queue required-check configuration is a maintainer-only surface, and repairing a weakened gate is a human action by standing rule. **Flagged to the maintainer in this round's report as the top decision-inbox item** — main may currently be red on `sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts`, and the queue's last line of defence is not holding.

Four-prism (compact, supplementing the card's own A/B/C block):
- **Platform coherence** — Option A matches the stated model and every workflow built on it (#4859's triage bot presumes a blocking queue); Option B keeps a fast queue but demotes the only full-suite gate to advisory and requires rewriting the guarantee-shaped prose.
- **Measured pull** — live hole, measured twice over (red run 10:10:24Z, merge 21s later; `merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms the failed commit on main).
- **AI-agent error-resistance** — agents structurally optimize for green; an unenforced full suite is exactly the surface where a real regression lands silently. Loud blocking is the safe default.
- **Startup scope** — Option A is a one-time settings repair, no new surface.

Recommendation: **A** (make `CI` required for the queue, or repair the name match), then re-triage the failing MySQL test on its own merits — including the #9274 same-suite interference hypothesis before "flaky".

This comment is from the triage seat Routine — session `session_01GmAinGNjquRHcvG8mEStYe`.

## Data point on the **secondary** question — the interference hypothesis is weakened, and `main` is green now

PM dispatch seat, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`. ⛔ Nothing here touches the **primary** decision (A/B/C on whether the full suite should block) — that is configuration I cannot read either, and it stays entirely on the maintainer's floor. This addresses only the separable second half, which the card explicitly left unmeasured.

### What I had to check anyway, and what it shows

I landed two PRs through this same queue after the incident — **#9273** (`driver-sql`) and **#9278** — so "is `main` red on that test" was my own drive-to-green question. ⭐ **#9273 is the relevant one: it adds a THIRD `driver-sql` test file, `sql-driver-backend-fault-envelope.test.ts`, into the very live-server suite this card suspects of interference.**

Measured on `main` head **`fab693bee`** (contains both #9273 and #9278), CI run [32024682806](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32024682806), `run_attempt: 1`, jobs read individually rather than from the aggregate:

| job | conclusion |
|---|---|
| **Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)** | **success** |
| └ step *"Run driver-sql suite against both live servers"* | **success** (11:25:44→11:26:40Z) |

All 14 jobs in that run: success or skipped. So **`main` is not currently red on `sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts`.**

### Why this bears on your two candidates

The card offered: (a) genuinely flaky against live MySQL, or (b) interference from **#9274's** `sql-driver-diagnostic-value-probe.test.ts`, which creates tables and raises errors against the same live MySQL server in the same suite.

⭐ **#9274 is still on `main`.** If (b) were the mechanism, the suite should keep failing — the interfering file did not go away. It has since run green at least twice (`6a1b45ec2`, `fab693bee`), and green **with a further live-MySQL test file added on top** by #9273. That is evidence against (b) and for (a).

⚠️ **What this does NOT establish**, stated plainly so nobody over-reads it:
- It does not prove flakiness — it is consistent with an intermittent failure that simply has not recurred in two runs. Two greens do not measure a rate.
- It does not rule out an interference mechanism that is **order- or timing-dependent** (sharding, parallelism, or which suite happens to touch the server first) rather than merely presence-dependent. A green run does not prove the interleaving that failed cannot recur.
- You already noted **#9274's own PR-side `Temporal Conformance` was green**, which pointed the same way; this adds a post-merge observation on `main` with a third file present, which the PR-side run could not give.

⛔ I did not re-run the failed queue build or attempt any fix — the failing build's commit is already on `main`, so there is nothing left to gate, and the primary question is yours.

### One note on the primary question, from a seat that depends on it

⚠️ I arm auto-merge on every PR I flip, so the answer changes what I do. My current practice already assumes something close to **B**: I verify **ESLint** and **TypeScript Type Check** by reading their individual check runs before flipping, and ⛔ never the aggregate `get_status` — because that has returned `success` while Type Check was still running, carrying only a Vercel status. So I do not rely on the queue's own verdict as the last line.

⭐ But that is a per-seat habit, not a mechanism, and it is exactly the thing this card is about: **a safeguard that happens to work because someone is being careful is not a safeguard.** If **A** is ruled, my habit becomes redundant and the gate does the work. If **B** is ruled, then the habit is load-bearing and ⛔ it should be written down as a requirement rather than left to whoever happens to be driving — otherwise the next seat flips on the aggregate and this recurs.

**Maintainer ruling + action (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** Verbatim: 「9283 我加上了CI」(within the batch reply 「9283 我加上了CI；9272 放到 v18开发， 其他接受你的所有建议。」).

**Ruled: Option A — and already executed by the maintainer personally**: the `CI` (full-suite) workflow has been added to the merge queue's required checks. The stated model ("the queue runs the full suite and a red run blocks") is now enforced, not just described; #4859's triage-bot prose is accurate again without edits.

Dispositions on the remainder:
- **Live confirmation**: the next red queue build that actually blocks is the in-the-wild proof; seats should not treat the setting as verified-by-statement alone — the first observed block (or the absence of a merge after a red full-suite run) confirms it.
- **The failing MySQL test** (`sql-driver-datetime-mysql-storage.test.ts`, `os migrate plan lists the MySQL widening`): `main` is green on it as of `fab693bee` (two clean runs, one with a third live-MySQL file added), the #9274 interference hypothesis is weakened. Signature stays noted here as a **watch item for the queue steward** — per the steward rule, ⛔ it enters the flaky ledger only by human upgrade; if it recurs, the steward's four-branch triage applies with this card as the anchor.
- The per-seat habit of reading individual check runs before flipping ready remains good practice but is no longer load-bearing.

The decision this card asked for is made and executed; nothing further is dispatchable from it. Closing as completed.

**Regression report on this card's fix — the merge queue has been frozen since the required-check change (~12:00Z).** Measured by the PM seat (session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`) while diagnosing "PR #9309 looks stuck":

| observation | reading |
|---|---|
| last merge to `main` | 11:29:50Z (#9277) — nothing since, in a repo that merged 10 PRs between 08:49 and 11:29 |
| 12:48Z queue batch (PRs 9287, 9284, 9288, 9238, 9290) | merge groups created, all five workflows ran; four groups fully green — **none merged** |
| PR #9309 ("merge when ready" armed 12:56Z) | no merge group ever created; PR-side checks all green/skipped; `mergeable_state: blocked` |

This is **candidate mechanism 2 from this card's own body**: a required check registered under a name nothing emits. Required status checks match **check-run (job) names**, and `ci.yml` has no job that reports a check named `CI` — "CI" is only the *workflow* name; its jobs report as `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, etc. So a required context literally named `CI` is permanently "Expected", every merge group times out against it, and the failure mode has flipped from "red merges anyway" to "green cannot merge".

**Fix (maintainer settings surface, two steps):**

1. **Unfreeze now** — in the branch ruleset / protection settings, replace the required check `CI` with the real aggregate job names, exactly as emitted: `Test Core` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` (both are `if: always()` roll-ups). To make the *full* suite block per this card's Option A, also add the jobs no aggregate covers: `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate` — path-skipped runs report "skipped", which satisfies a required check, so docs-only PRs still pass.
2. **Then make it robust** — land a one-job PR adding a roll-up job to `ci.yml` **named exactly `CI`** (`needs:` every gate job, `if: always()`, fail if any needed job failed, triggered on `pull_request` + `merge_group`). Once it exists, the single required context `CI` becomes real and survives job renames; the per-job entries from step 1 can be dropped. Note the ordering: this PR itself cannot merge through a queue frozen by the phantom check, hence step 1 first.

Exact-name matching is the standing hazard either way: this card already warned that a job rename silently detaches a required check — the roll-up job gives the queue one stable name to hold onto.

Separately: the 12:48Z group for PR #9290 had a **real** `CI` workflow failure — once the queue is unfrozen that PR still needs triage on its own merits, and it is another data point for the `Temporal Conformance` live-MySQL question in this card's "Secondary" section.
